conventions.convention: Λ(θ) is minus the improper integral of log|2 sin u| from 0 to θ.
Positive tetrahedron shapes have Im z > 0; the three parameters are z, 1/(1-z), and (z-1)/z. A cusp path contributes a corner parameter on its left and its reciprocal on its right.
The upper half-space metric is t⁻²(dx²+dy²+dt²); a translation lattice at height R gives cusp volume equal to its coordinate fundamental area divided by 2R².
Rigidity assumes full AC, complete finite-volume curvature-minus-one metrics, and fundamental-group isomorphisms considered up to basepoint conjugacy. The realizing isometry may reverse orientation.

Hyperbolization requires irreducibility, incompressible boundary, embedded-torus atoroidality, and exclusion of Seifert fibrations; the deep hyperbolization and torus-theorem inputs are explicitly external.
The figure-eight knot is the oriented closure of (σ₁σ₂⁻¹)², with the displayed face maps, edge classes, and cusp-basis corner traces.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For nonempty connected oriented complete finite-volume Riemannian three-manifolds of constant curvature -1, every fundamental-group isomorphism, up to basepoint conjugacy, is induced by a unique isometry. It is properly homotopic to every proper homotopy equivalence inducing that outer isomorphism, agrees with its orientation, and preserves volume.

Assume AC. Every nonempty connected oriented complete finite-volume curvature-minus-one three-manifold is a compact core together with finitely many pairwise disjoint standard rank-two torus cusp ends. Zero cusps are allowed.

Assume AC. If Γ ≤ PSL₂(C) is discrete with finite nonzero Haar quotient measure and an orientation-preserving quasiconformal sphere homeomorphism h satisfies hγ = θ(γ)h for a homomorphism θ:Γ→PSL₂(C), then h is Möbius.

Assume AC. A quasi-isometry of hyperbolic three-space induces an ideal-boundary homeomorphism with a uniform all-circle distortion bound after normalization at infinity. It is analytically quasiconformal when orientation-preserving, and becomes so after reflection when orientation-reversing; equivariance passes to the boundary.

Assume AC. A compact connected orientable smooth knot exterior with one torus boundary component, irreducible, boundary-incompressible, atoroidal and not Seifert-fibered, has interior admitting a complete finite-volume curvature-minus-one metric with one torus cusp.

The displayed two-tetrahedron figure-eight face gluing, with all six shape parameters equal to exp(iπ/3), has edge products and basis cusp multipliers equal to 1 and angle sums 2π, giving a complete finite-volume metric with one peripheral torus cusp.
Every regular ideal tetrahedron in hyperbolic three-space has volume v₃ = 3Λ(π/3), equal to the displayed positive series.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 writes the integral of t⁻³ as A[1/(2t²)] from 1 to infinity and then A/2. That bracket evaluates to -A/2; the antiderivative needs a minus sign. The stated positive volume is correct.

The multiplier is defined for 'an oriented path' by its encountered corners, without requiring a transverse normal path or specifying passage to such a representative. Paths through link vertices or along link edges have no specified corner sequence. Purcell Definition 4.12 explicitly first homotopes a loop so each triangle segment cuts off one corner. The normal-path convention should be stated.

Fact L1 and Proof 1.1 refer to 'the countable-choice assumption of [F1]'. F1 cites def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system, whose Definition has no countable-choice assumption. The relevant choice hypothesis belongs to the geometric suppliers behind F2; the proof's application of F2 itself is sound.

seams_checked.note: Chosen compact exteriors, peripheral tori and nontrivial-knot hypotheses match the opened supplier interfaces. Full AC in the consuming topological results supplies the suppliers' countable-choice hypotheses.

The actual uses are the definitions of irreducibility, incompressibility, embedded-torus atoroidality and Seifert fibrations. Hyperbolization explicitly imports the additional torus-theorem comparison; it does not infer hyperbolicity merely from the JSJ vocabulary.

Opened citing passages use the proved quotient/cusp decomposition, shape-angle relations and volume conventions faithfully. The multicusp gluing lemma explicitly reconstructs the cusp argument separately at each vertex rather than applying the one-vertex criterion beyond its stated domain.

The open-problem formulation supplies a complete finite-volume metric with one peripheral torus cusp and explicitly defines its Riemannian volume. It asserts no hyperbolization or asymptotic theorem from the geometric supplier.
